source.instructions: Mining Market Research is a read-only stock screening and analysis service. In public access mode no login is required; all callers share global rate and concurrency limits. Full market datasets may be used for server-side filtering and aggregate analysis. Price history is stored in stock_daily; discover markets with get_available_exchanges and trading dates with get_available_dates. list_stock_tables lists distinct physical tables. Row-level results shown to the host are limited to 200 rows per call and may continue only through the returned short-lived opaque cursor. Restricted mode allows at most 1,000 browsed rows per registered query; bulk mode allows continuation within its 200,000-row hard result limit. A Top-N value bounds the complete logical analysis and CSV result, not the display page. User-authored SQL OFFSET remains forbidden; SQL continuation requires an explicit stable ORDER BY. When next_cursor is present, tell the user which rows are shown and offer the next page; do not traverse many pages unless the user asks. CSV eligibility and file limits are controlled by the active server data policy and are returned in each rowset's export_policy. When restrictions are enabled, never reconstruct a dataset by splitting filters, dates, fields, or sort ranges. When bulk mode is enabled, complete structured screens and previously validated bounded or aggregate SQL results may be downloaded within the reported hard limits. If export is refused, continue with server-side analysis or suggest a compatible query. CSV download URLs are bearer capabilities and must not be shared. Before stock-data or company-report calls, resolve a company name or ticker to exchange, ticker, and company name; use chat context and primary web sources to disambiguate when needed. For company reports use get_company_report in auto mode first. Display valid existing English research with its ORIGINAL generation date, translate faithfully for the user's language, and ask whether to refresh. A translation is not new research; never add new facts to it. When the result is generation_ready, perform live web research immediately without mentioning expired or missing reports. User requests for updated research use refresh mode or prepare_company_report_generation directly. These return prompts, not finished reports. If live web research is unavailable, explain that limitation. Never upload, save or persist generated reports or translations. When working from news, pass up to five relevant news_codes and the user's research_focus; confirm the target company if there are multiple candidates. External, inactive, delisted and unmatched companies use Others and require identity and listing-status verification. ETF and fund instruments are not eligible. For news questions, put the user utterance and English search terms in search_news.q, stay inside the current NEWS_ACCESS option, review headline cards first, and fetch at most five full articles with get_news_article for one user question. Mining and covered news options follow the dynamic exchange catalog. An empty news result means no matching articles, not an unsupported exchange. Explicit invalid or out-of-policy filters reject the search without dropping them. Search the local corpus before asking the host to browse; prepare_news_web_research only prepares a prompt and does not fetch pages. Connection status reports only service access, authentication state, published limits, the active data policy, and the current news access option. Never ask users to paste credentials or tokens into chat.

tools.name: get_connection_status
tools.title: Get Mining Market Research connection status
tools.description: Use this when you need to check whether Mining Market Research public access is available, whether sign-in is required, the published service limits, the active data policy, or the current news access option. It does not query stock or news data.

inputSchema.description: No arguments. Returns the current connection status.

name.description: Current NEWS_ACCESS option name. Callers cannot change it.

filters.description: Expanded tag ceiling for the current option.

kind.description: News tag kind this filter applies to.

values.description: Allowed values for this kind, including exchange aliases.

epoch.description: Opaque news-access epoch. Rotates when the option changes.

annotations.title: Get Mining Market Research connection status

exchanges.description: One or more uppercase exchange codes from get_available_exchanges.

tables.description: One to 100 exact table names returned by list_stock_tables.

tools.name: screen_stocks
tools.title: Screen stocks
tools.description: Use this when you need structured stock filters and sorting; prefer it over raw SQL when the requested fields and operators fit this schema. It returns at most 200 rows per call and an opaque cursor when another display page is available. For company prices, resolve company identity first. Batch stocks on the same exchange with a TICKER in filter and request only the fields needed. Use as_of_date for one day or start_date/end_date for history; do not issue one call per stock/day. All dates use the unified stock_daily table. For a cross-market portfolio, use instruments to bind each ticker to its exchange in one request. Do not combine instruments with exchanges. Additional filters narrow the selected instruments.

instruments.description: Optional exact exchange/ticker pairs from resolve_company_identity. Use instead of exchanges for a cross-market portfolio. Other filters are ANDed with these pairs. Omit on cursor continuation; base_query_id refinements preserve the original pairs and cannot replace them.

items.description: Uppercase exchange code returned by get_available_exchanges.

exchanges.description: Optional markets to screen. Omit or pass an empty array to use every available exchange.

as_of_date.description: Optional exact market-data date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Omit or pass null to use each exchange's latest available table.

start_date.description: Optional inclusive start date. Cannot be combined with as_of_date.

end_date.description: Optional inclusive end date. Cannot be combined with as_of_date.

fields.description: Optional output fields. CSV export requires an explicit list; EXCHANGE, Date, and TICKER are always included and count toward export limits.

filters.description: Zero to 30 AND-combined filters. Field names must exactly match get_stock_schema for every selected exchange.

field.description: Exact stock column name returned by get_stock_schema, for example Price_Close or TICKER.

operator.description: Comparison operator. Use in with 1..100 values and between with exactly two ordered values.

value.description: Comparison value for this filter. Use one scalar for eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte; null is allowed only with eq or ne. Use an array of 1..100 scalars for in, and exactly two ordered scalars for between.

items.description: One allowlisted field comparison used in the stock screen.

sort.description: Optional ordered sort keys. Fields must match get_stock_schema for every selected exchange.

field.description: Exact stock column name returned by get_stock_schema.

direction.description: Sort direction; defaults to asc when omitted.

items.description: One sort key, evaluated in array order.

top_n.description: Optional global Top-N bound after sorting. This controls the logical analysis and CSV result, not the per-call display page. Restricted mode allows at most 200; bulk mode allows up to the 200,000-row file limit.

base_query_id.description: Optional prior screen_stocks query_id to refine. New filters are ANDed with the encrypted original query and reuse its exact physical partitions.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor returned by the immediately preceding page of the same tool. Omit or pass null for the first page; never construct or edit this value.

page_size.description: Maximum rows to return on this page. Defaults to 200.

inputSchema.description: Build a safe stock screen using documented fields, structured comparisons, and cursor-based display pages of at most 200 rows. On continuation, send only the opaque cursor and optional page_size. Export eligibility is returned by the active server data policy.

eligible_by_query.description: Provisional when total count is unknown; export replay checks all resource limits.

next_cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor returned by the immediately preceding page of the same tool. Omit or pass null for the first page; never construct or edit this value.

tools.name: validate_readonly_sql
tools.title: Validate read-only SQL
tools.description: Use this when you need to check one proposed SELECT or WITH...SELECT before execution; it never runs the statement.

sql.description: Exactly one SELECT or WITH...SELECT statement using allowlisted stock tables. Double-quoted allowlisted table names are normalized to MySQL backticks; string values are unchanged. DDL, DML, comments, and multiple statements are rejected.
examples: SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM stock_daily

inputSchema.description: Validate one read-only SQL statement without executing it.

tools.name: run_readonly_sql
tools.title: Run bounded read-only SQL
tools.description: Use this when structured screen_stocks cannot express the analysis; it executes one allowlisted read-only SELECT for aggregate or bounded-ticker analysis. The active data policy decides whether its registered result may be exported. Include a stable ORDER BY when a multi-page row result may be needed.

sql.description: Exactly one SELECT or WITH...SELECT statement using table names from list_stock_tables and columns from get_table_schema. Double-quoted allowlisted table names are normalized to MySQL backticks before execution; string values are unchanged.
examples: SELECT symbol, raw_close FROM stock_daily WHERE exchange = 'ASX' AND symbol = 'BHP' AND trade_date = '2026-07-15' ORDER BY trade_date, symbol

max_rows.description: Maximum rows returned on this display page. Defaults to and cannot exceed 200. This does not change the logical SQL result.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor returned by the immediately preceding page of the same tool. Omit or pass null for the first page; never construct or edit this value.

inputSchema.description: Execute one allowlisted read-only SQL query and return a query_id plus a cursor-based display page of at most 200 rows. Supply sql on the first call. On continuation, send only the opaque cursor and optional max_rows. A bulk-enabled server may export the same validated query through its query_id.

eligible_by_query.description: Provisional when total count is unknown; export replay checks all resource limits.

next_cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor returned by the immediately preceding page of the same tool. Omit or pass null for the first page; never construct or edit this value.

tools.name: resolve_company_identity
tools.title: Resolve company identity
tools.description: Use this when the user supplies a company name or ticker and you need a canonical exchange, ticker, and company name before calling stock-data or company-report tools. It searches only the dynamically discovered exchange master tables. Exact unique matches are resolved; cross-market, share-class, prefix, and contains matches remain ambiguous.

query.description: Company name or ticker extracted from the user's request or prior chat context. Do not send the full conversation.

exchange_hint.description: Optional exchange code established from chat context or public-source verification. Codes outside the discovered markets are accepted but produce not_found_in_supported_markets.

purpose.description: Downstream use for the identity. Defaults to stock_data and does not change matching rules.

inputSchema.description: Resolve a company name or ticker against dynamically discovered masters before using the canonical identity downstream.

tools.name: get_company_report
tools.title: Get company report or prepare live research
tools.description: Use this when the user asks for company research, including from a news article. Auto returns an existing English report less than seven days old, with its original date. Translate faithfully without adding facts or labelling translation as new research, then ask whether to refresh. Otherwise immediately execute the returned live-research prompt; Do not mention expired reports. Refresh skips existing reports on user request. Never save generated research or translations. News IDs additionally require news.read.

ticker.description: Verified current or historical ticker using letters, numbers, dots, hyphens, underscores, or slashes.

company_name.description: Verified legal or commonly published company name corresponding to the exchange and ticker.

output_locale.description: Required BCP-47 language tag for the generated summary and section bodies. Fixed labels and the seven section headings remain English.

news_codes.description: Up to five accessible news IDs linked to this issuer; requires news.read.

research_focus.description: The user's research question, retained when refreshing the report.

mode.description: Auto displays valid English research; refresh skips lookup when the user asks for new research.

tools.name: list_news_filters
tools.title: List news filters
tools.description: Use this when you need the official English news tag and exchange values allowed by the current NEWS_ACCESS option before calling search_news. It returns a facet word list, not synonyms; map user language onto these values yourself. Exchange facets reflect existing articles; news_policy reports the allowed scope. A missing facet does not mean the exchange is unsupported.

inputSchema.description: No arguments. Returns the current news option and allowed facets.

news_policy.description: Current NEWS_ACCESS option, expanded filters, and epoch.

name.description: Current NEWS_ACCESS option name. Callers cannot change it.

filters.description: Expanded tag ceiling for the current option.

kind.description: News tag kind this filter applies to.

values.description: Allowed values for this kind, including exchange aliases.

epoch.description: Opaque news-access epoch. Rotates when the option changes.

exchanges.description: Canonical exchanges with articles visible under the current option.

metals.description: Official metal tag values visible under the current option.

events.description: Official event tag values visible under the current option.

geographies.description: Official geography tag values visible under the current option.

sources.description: Source slugs present in the visible news corpus.

tools.name: search_news
tools.title: Search news
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about mining, exchange, or company news. Put the user utterance and English search terms in q. Invalid or out-of-scope filters reject the query without dropping them. Returns headline cards only; pick at most five articles and call get_news_article for those. Do not fetch every card. Articles without a company_type tag are excluded when the current option requires MINING.

q.description: User utterance plus English search terms. The server tokenizes this string; Chinese tokens are not sent to the article body index.
examples: 上周黄金钻探 gold drill

tags.description: Optional official tag values copied from list_news_filters. Matching is case-insensitive. Values outside the current NEWS_ACCESS ceiling reject the query. Facet titles such as Drill Results are accepted.

exchanges.description: Optional exchange codes used to narrow within the current option. Codes outside the option reject the query; filters are never dropped.

exchange.description: Optional issuer exchange from resolve_company_identity. Must be paired with ticker. Rejected when outside the current option.

ticker.description: Optional issuer ticker from resolve_company_identity. Must be paired with exchange.

start_date.description: Optional inclusive published-date lower bound in YYYY-MM-DD. The window cannot exceed 365 days.

end_date.description: Optional inclusive published-date upper bound in YYYY-MM-DD. The window cannot exceed 365 days.

page_size.description: Cards to return on this page. Defaults to 20 and cannot exceed 50.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor returned by the immediately preceding page of the same tool. Omit or pass null for the first page; never construct or edit this value.

inputSchema.description: Search the news corpus inside the current NEWS_ACCESS ceiling. On continuation send only the opaque cursor and optional page_size.

companies.description: Companies resolved from ticker tags and actual master records; never guess missing identities.

news_code.description: Stable article identifier used by get_news_article.

summary.description: Short standfirst or excerpt. Never the full body.

tags.description: Displayed tag values for this article.

source_url.description: Original public article URL when it is a safe http(s) link.

items.description: Headline cards for this page. Bodies are omitted.

interpretation.description: How the server interpreted q, tags, and exchanges.

accepted_tags.description: Tags kept after NEWS_ACCESS validation. Matching is case-insensitive; values are returned in lowercase.

ignored_tags.description: Unknown or out-of-scope tags that were dropped.

content_terms.description: Tokenized query terms used for full-text matching.

fulltext_skipped.description: True when q produced no usable tokens and latest-in-option was used.

applied_option.description: NEWS_ACCESS option name applied to this search.

next_cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor returned by the immediately preceding page of the same tool. Omit or pass null for the first page; never construct or edit this value.

tools.title: Get news article

body_text.description: Truncated plain-text body. Markup is stripped.

source_url.description: Original public article URL when it is a safe http(s) link.

content_truncated.description: True when body_text was cut to the 20,000-character limit.
